title: The Meal Mill — below the south bridge, Sill
caption: The water-mill under the south bridge, drawn at the scale of a sack set against the hopper: the Ilm coming down from the Cross with its silt shoals and tide ripples, the timber bridge, the race taking water from above the mill and the tail returning it below, the great wheel with its paddles and spokes, the two dressed millstones under the roof, the hopper with barley going in, the meal-book kept by the miller's daughter with a barleycorn shut in its fold, the toll-bag, the sacks white with mill-dust, the grey print at the corner nobody will own, and the brown silt tideline the flood left along the foot of the leaf. The Cross and Slate Row stand faint on the north bank, High Kiln above them, Low Kiln with the Vail roof and the yard well across the water, the worked strips at the east edge. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Ash, with compass, a scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the mill keeping one hour and the stone another, the figures that go into the meal and leave nothing on the leaf, the early note entered nil in a factor's clerk's narrow hand, the foundling left at the mill with a stone under him and no name, and the crust that travels two inches from a boy's ear. An engraved barleycorn and an engraved dressing-pick sit in the margin.
